record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: For the nonlinear evolution ∂_t f(z,t) = z f′(z,t) ∫_T ((z+ζ)/(z-ζ)) |dζ| / |f′(ζ,t)|^α, how do the dynamics for α > 0 differ qualitatively from those for α < 0, especially with respect to concentration of growth near inward- versus outward-pointing singular features and possible singularity formation?

evidence.quote: How do the evolutions obtained when α > 0 and α < 0 differ qualitatively from each other?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{T}=\partial\mathbb{D}$ the unit circle, and $|d\zeta|$ the arc-length measure on $\mathbb{T}$. For a real parameter $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, consider the nonlinear, nonlocal evolution equation for a one-parameter family of conformal maps $f(\cdot,t):\mathbb{D}\to\Omega(t)\subset\mathbb{C}$,
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}(z,t)\;=\;z\,f'(z,t)\,\int_{\mathbb{T}}\frac{z+\zeta}{z-\zeta}\,\frac{|d\zeta|}{|f'(\zeta,t)|^{\alpha}},\qquad z\in\mathbb{D},$$
where $f'$ denotes the derivative in $z$ and the boundary values $|f'(\zeta,t)|$ are taken in a suitable nontangential sense. Starting from a smooth univalent initial datum $f(z,0)$, analyze and contrast the qualitative behavior of the solutions for $\alpha>0$ versus $\alpha<0$. In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Determine, in each sign regime, whether the boundary growth concentrates near points where $|f'(\zeta,t)|$ is small (corresponding to inward-pointing/cusp-like features of $\partial\Omega(t)$) or near points where $|f'(\zeta,t)|$ is large (corresponding to outward-pointing/protrusion features).
\item Establish whether, and in what sense, finite-time singularities (loss of univalence, cusp formation, or blow-up of curvature) can form, and characterize the asymptotic shape of $\Omega(t)$ as such a singularity is approached.
\item Identify any conserved or monotone quantities (e.g., area, capacity, or weighted moments) that distinguish the two regimes.
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open qualitative comparison for a family of nonlinear, nonlocal Loewner-type evolutions related to Hele-Shaw / Laplacian-growth models. Related work (e.g., Constantin–Elgindi–Nguyen–Vicol on singularity formation in a Hele-Shaw model) addresses singularity formation in specific Hele-Shaw settings but does not resolve the qualitative comparison between $\alpha>0$ and $\alpha<0$ regimes for this particular nonlocal evolution. No publication establishing a complete qualitative classification was located.

status_evidence.title: On Singularity Formation in a Hele-Shaw Model
status_evidence.snippet: Studies pinch-off / finite-time singularity formation in a lubrication-type Hele-Shaw model.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not directly address the alpha>0 vs alpha<0 comparison for the stated nonlocal Loewner-type evolution.

status_evidence.title: Finite-time singularity formation in Hele-Shaw systems
status_evidence.snippet: Demonstrates finite-time singularities in Hele-Shaw interface dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Provides context on singularity formation in related interface dynamics but not a resolution of this question.
